title: Row marginal of the joint Rademacher measure
statement: Fix natural numbers $k$ and $d$ and a row index $i \in \{0, \dots, k-1\}$, and consider the joint measure on the set of $k \times d$ real arrays under which all $k \cdot d$ entries are independent Rademacher variables, each taking the values $-1$ and $+1$ with probability $\tfrac12$ apiece. Then the pushforward of this measure along the map that sends an array to its $i$-th row, an element of $\mathbb{R}^d$, equals the $d$-fold product $\bigotimes_{j=1}^{d} \mathrm{Rad}$ of Rademacher distributions.
hypotheses_covered: k and d are natural numbers
i is a row index in {0, ..., k-1}
joint measure is the i.i.d. Rademacher product over all k×d entries
replaced:
The pushforward of the joint measure along the $i$-th row projection
$\omega \mapsto \omega_i$ equals the product measure
$\bigotimes_{j \in \mathrm{Fin}\,d} \mathrm{Rad}$.
